decisions.title: Preferred strict JSON Schema sampling for workflow tools
decisions.rationale: Pi 0.82 adds capability-gated constrained JSON Schema sampling, and ce-workflow registers thirteen nested workflow tools in extensions/work-models.js. Using strict=prefer improves argument reliability on supporting models while preserving fallback behavior everywhere else.
decisions.verification: node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs passed and asserts all 13 registered tools use constrainedSampling { type: json_schema, strict: prefer }; primary LSP diagnostics reported no errors; npm run verify:quiet passed

decisions.title: Session-aware and streaming bash runtime metadata
decisions.rationale: Pi now supplies session/model environment variables to built-in and factory bash tools and streams direct RPC bash updates. ce-workflow uses Pi's built-in bash/tool lifecycle and its evaluation RPC client already consumes correlated RPC events, so it inherits the capability without a repository adapter.

decisions.title: Provider, model catalog, thinking, authentication, and renderer additions
decisions.rationale: OpenRouter/Kimi login, Claude Opus 5 and xhigh metadata, Anthropic gateway auth, model-catalog refreshes, and outputPad affect host/provider or custom-renderer surfaces. ce-workflow registers no provider or custom message renderer and already queries the host model registry and applied thinking level.

decisions.title: Inherited runtime and lifecycle fixes
decisions.rationale: Retry, compaction routing, context discovery, editor, scoped-model, startup-resource, and TUI fixes are internal Pi behavior. The extension hooks used by ce-workflow remain additive and supported, so the installed host supplies these fixes without compatibility code.

decisions.title: Project-grounded proactive catch-up verdicts
decisions.rationale: ce-pov turns upstream release notes into repository-specific adoption decisions before the baseline advances.
decisions.verification: work-catch-up objective and completion-gate tests passed

decisions.title: Technical explainers for difficult adoption choices
decisions.rationale: ce-explain is useful only when a candidate cannot be decided from the compact POV summary.
decisions.verification: work-catch-up objective test covers conditional ce-explain guidance

decisions.title: Recurring external feedback sweep
decisions.rationale: ce-sweep overlaps the native work-item and improvement-reporting flow until Slack, GitHub Issues, or email ingestion is explicitly configured.

decisions.title: Versioned agent contracts and side-effect-free launch preflight
decisions.rationale: ce-workflow's extension-owned RPC handoff already validates through the same spawn resolver, records a task only after acknowledged launch, disables plugin acceptance with a reason, and applies native work-item gates. Adding a second preflight or agentContract v1 projection would duplicate controls without changing a current decision or failure path.

decisions.title: Capability ceilings and shared child extension defaults
decisions.rationale: Every packaged ce-workflow role already declares an explicit strict tool allowlist, context mode, skill inheritance, and thinking level in agents/*.md. A global capability ceiling or defaultExtensions/defaultThinking layer would duplicate those fail-closed role contracts rather than simplify them.

decisions.title: Evidence and independent-review semantics
decisions.rationale: 0.37 separates verified evidence from achieved independent review. ce-workflow already sends reason-bearing acceptance level none for direct role handoffs, orchestrates work-reviewer separately, and its active guidance says evidence ends at verified and review is orthogonal, so no compatibility edit is needed.

decisions.title: Fleet, async terminal proof, steering, and worktree handoff manifests
decisions.rationale: The persistent FleetView, exact wait/steer wakeups, durable process-terminal state, Windows resilience, and status projections are supplied by pi-subagents itself and directly improve ce-workflow's existing async RPC handoffs. Aggregate worktree manifests do not apply because ce-workflow deliberately keeps one writer and does not launch parallel worktree writers.

decisions.title: Delegation v2 and structured foreground leaves
decisions.rationale: ce-workflow needs durable async specialist runs with supervisor coordination and native work-item state, while delegation v2 is an extension-owned concurrent foreground leaf contract. Replacing the existing async spawn RPC would lose the lifecycle shape this repository relies on.

decisions.title: Selective optional comments
decisions.rationale: Planning and adoption choices benefit from caveats, while destructive binary approvals must explicitly disable comments.
decisions.verification: open-question, work-goal, and dirty-recovery tests passed

decisions.title: Diagnostic disposition tool
decisions.rationale: pi-lens now registers lens_diagnostic_mark as a situational tool and honors its marks across diagnostics (upstream docs/dispositions.md). The host exposes it automatically through pi_lens_activate_tools, while ce-workflow's verifier triage covers a separate review-finding store, so duplicate integration would add no value.

decisions.title: Deferred formatter and autofix bus signals
decisions.rationale: The new pilens:format:queued, pilens:format:start, and pilens:autofix:start events are useful only for an in-process immutable-snapshot listener. ce-workflow schedules background verification from an explicit settled checkpoint in extensions/work-models.js rather than snapshotting during deferred lens mutation, so there is no current race to fix.

decisions.title: Cached workspace diagnostics and scan correctness fixes
decisions.rationale: Persisted LSP sweep caching, tracked-file discovery, source-twin resolution, deduplication, and warm-up timeout fixes are internal pi-lens behavior (upstream CHANGELOG.md); ce-workflow already calls the public lens diagnostics tools and inherits the faster, quieter results automatically.

decisions.title: Optional ty server and human project map
decisions.rationale: ty is a PATH-only fallback selected inside pi-lens and /lens-map is a human-only command with no agent tool. Neither has a ce-workflow call site or requires repository configuration.
